requirements.requirement: Publish node2's HTTP service (port 8080) on TCP port 80 of node1's outward-facing address (the address node1 presents on the shared private network)
requirements.summary: A DNAT rule was added to node1's config.xml forwarding tcp/80 on 10.100.216.10 (node1's LAN address) to 10.100.216.11:8080, confirmed live in `pfctl -s nat` after filter reload, and end-to-end curl to http://10.100.216.10/ returned HTTP 200 with node2's service body.

requirements.requirement: node3 (on the same private network as node2) reaches the service through node1's address rather than by contacting node2 directly
requirements.summary: Initial attempts failed with a TCP RST because reflected replies bypassed node1 and went straight from node2 to node3's real IP (shown via parallel tcpdump on node1/node2). Enabling OPNsense's NAT reflection helper added a source-NAT/masquerade rule so node2's reply traverses node1; curl from node3 to http://10.100.216.10/ then returned HTTP 200 with node2's content, and this was re-verified after each node's restart.

requirements.requirement: An HTTP service is actually running on node2:8080 to be published (implicit prerequisite of the task)
requirements.summary: Discovery showed no HTTP service existed on node2 before the executor's work; a persistent systemd unit (hairpin-demo.service, python3 http.server bound to 0.0.0.0:8080) was created, enabled, and verified serving content locally and on node2's LAN IP, and confirmed still active after node2's own restart.

requirements.requirement: No collateral loss of node1 management access (SSH/webgui) while modifying the firewall/NAT configuration
requirements.summary: sshd remained listening on :22 and node1's own HTTPS webgui remained reachable (200) throughout and after the config.xml edits and filter reloads; the executor's exec channel to node1 was never lost during configuration (only during the deliberate later reboot).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/NAT/connectivity state on all three managed nodes
requirements.summary: For each node the executor captured a pre-restart boot identity and healthy functional baseline, issued the restart, observed the connection drop, then confirmed a changed boot identity (node1 kern.boottime 17:51:16->17:59:12; node2 boot_id 8d1d94e2->a82fbb2d; node3 boot_id cfdbaef8->f85b9984) and recovered state: node1's NAT rules and sshd, node2's hairpin-demo.service auto-start, and node3's hairpin path (200) and direct node2 access (200). The fixed lifecycle after_executor snapshot independently corroborates all three boot-identity changes and node2's now-listening 8080 socket.

overall_summary: The executor stood up the missing HTTP service on node2, published it on node1's port 80 via a DNAT rule, and correctly diagnosed and resolved two real obstacles (anti-lockout redirect intercepting port 80, and asymmetric hairpin return traffic) using firewall-native mechanisms (disablehttpredirect, NAT reflection helper). End-to-end functional proof shows node3 reaching the service through node1's address with a 200 response and matching body, and SSH/webgui access to node1 was preserved throughout. All three nodes were restarted per the mandatory protocol with clear boot-identity changes and full functional recovery, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots.
limitations: No evidence was captured of node3 accessing node2 directly being blocked or discouraged after the fix — the task only requires that node3 reach the service via node1's address, which was demonstrated, but the executor's own note that direct node2:8080 access 'still also works' means the private network is not otherwise segmented; this is consistent with the plain reading of the task and not treated as a shortfall here.

The dhclient vtnet1 mutation on node1's final state (e.g., whether the interface retained a DHCP lease) was not re-verified after the fact in the captured evidence, so its persistence and possible incidental effects on node1 could not be independently confirmed beyond the initial command output.
Config.xml backup files (.bak, .bak2, .bak3) were not observed to be cleaned up; their final presence/absence was not directly checked in later evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands were directly tied to the task: config.xml edits for the DNAT/reflection rules and the two follow-on fixes (disablehttpredirect, enablenatreflectionhelper) were each diagnosed with clear cause-and-effect evidence (pfctl output, tcpdump captures) before being applied, and each config.xml write was preceded by a backup copy (.bak, .bak2, .bak3) and validated with xmllint before reload. One unnecessary mutation stands out: cmd-a6f4ed86418448c8 ran `dhclient -b vtnet1` on node1, bringing up DHCP on a second NIC (vtnet1) that was never referenced by the final DNAT/reflection configuration (which used only vtnet0/10.100.216.10) or by any subsequent command in the trace — this appears to be an abandoned troubleshooting probe and was left in place (no evidence it was reverted). The three config.xml backup files left on node1 (config.xml.bak/.bak2/.bak3) are low-risk residue but were not cleaned up. The systemd unit and /srv/www content on node2 are appropriate persistent residue since standing up the port-8080 service was a legitimate part of the task. Reboots were issued deliberately and are within the mandated restart protocol, not incidental mutations.
